items.q: What should you remember about peak?
items.a: real estate + related ~**¼ of China's GDP**; **70%** of household wealth in housing; **22%** of urban households owned multiple homes.

items.q: Why does this matter: **three red lines housing policy** shut developer financing → Evergrande liquidation / Country Garden defaults?
items.a: **three red lines housing policy** shut developer financing → Evergrande liquidation / Country Garden defaults → unfinished pre-sales → mortgage boycott threats (2022).

items.q: What should you remember about reverse feedback loop?
items.a: **stop buying → no** pre-sale cash → more stalled projects → more fear.

items.q: What should you remember about demographics amplify?
items.a: **aging, fewer marriages, slower** urbanization, tens of millions empty/unfinished units.

items.q: What should you remember about beijing response?
items.a: **7T yuan whitelist to finish projects, lower mortgage rates/down payments** — still expected further price falls before 2027.

items.q: Why does this matter: US banks largely **not** directly exposed; spillover via earnings, commodities (~50% world steel / ~60% cement?
items.a: US banks largely **not** directly exposed; spillover via earnings, commodities (~50% world steel / ~60% cement at peak China construction), export competition, USD strength.

items.q: What should you remember about uS vs China?
items.a: **concentration (25% vs 70%), supply (shortage** vs ghost cities), debt (fixed-rate equity-rich vs prepaid unfinished + leveraged developers).

items.q: What should you remember about **two americas housing**?
items.a: **Northeast/Midwest still hot; Texas/Florida/Mountain West** correcting; list prices down while sale prices hit records (expensive homes sell).

items.q: What should you remember about lesson?
items.a: **never let financial life** depend on a single asset, sector, or stock going up.
